title: RAW UNREVIEWED: a formulary alternates recipient clauses and compact patient nominals while preserving administration scope
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. A complete St Gall antidote interleaves recipient-class nominals and relative clauses before giving its base recipe. Explore a shared writing construction in which a condition may be expressed as a clause about a person or packed into a recipient nominal; changes of carrier remain attached to that recipient branch, not to a newly invented drug.

source.edition: Antidotarium Sangallense, Sigerist1923 pp78-79, online MediManus transcription
source.unit: Complete Incipit antidotum adrianum entry, ending before Antidotum dianacardon;262 whitespace-delimited words in the retained extraction
source.witness: Source identifies Cod.Sang.44 pp228-260 as9th century; no native manuscript collation in this pass
source.source_summary: One named antidote receives a series of recipient-conditioned administration instructions before its ingredient recipe. The list mixes patient-category words with relative clauses. A negative fever clause and a positive patient nominal accompany different carriers. Repeated references retain the antidote, but delivered mixtures and routes vary; one branch adds hyssop and oregano.
source.short_quote: qui non febriunt cum mulsa dabis, febricitantibus autem cum aqua calida ieiuno
source.uncertainties: The fever-positive clause may have narrower or broader recipient scope; do not silently make the whole list a disjoint or exhaustive decision table. Edition spelling, abbreviations and broken-word forms are retained. No quantities decoded or recomputed.

design.book_production_mechanism: A compiler assembles a named-compound monograph from administration cases and a formulation. Repeated case descriptions can alternate an expanded recipient clause with a compact condition-bearing nominal. Repetition may thus concern recipient types or administration frames rather than sequential material processing. This is an attested source organization with an unassessed extension to Voynich.
design.finite_construction: For anonymous preparation M and recipient x: a clause asserting condition P(x), or a nominal denoting a P-bearing recipient, supplies the same patient variable to GIVE(M,x,carrier C). Negation applies to P, not to M. The later base recipe defines M; it is not an instruction performed after every administration case. Delivered mixture M+C is distinct from M, and explicitly added branch ingredients are preserved.
rivals: CONDITION_NOMINAL: related forms encode an afflicted recipient versus a predication about that recipient.
MATERIAL_DERIVATION: related forms name different ingredients or their preparation states, so the continuation acts on materials rather than classifying recipients.
CHRONOLOGICAL_PROCESS: each case is a successive action on one material batch; this differs from multiple conditional uses of one named preparation.
design.unequal_written_consequence: A compact recipient nominal and its expanded relative-clause alternative must bind the same recipient slot and retain condition polarity and the carrier selection. A material reading instead binds an ingredient slot; a temporal process reading would wrongly consume all listed alternatives unless it independently marks branches. A shared constructor must work with a second predicate family, not only a chosen fever example. No allomorph may be introduced just to rescue a target occurrence.

actual_existing_target_nomination.smallest_action: After root selection, retrieve profiles for actual candidate whole forms and draft the full existing packet under one recipient-clause/nominal rule, keeping every unknown and the material alternative. A local branch can be a candidate construction before the whole paragraph is translated, but unknown surrounding content cannot count as confirming context.

design.positive_structure_used: Directed composition and whole-form residuals motivate testing a shared but lexically restricted nominalization; known-family transfer does not license new-stem generalization. Entry-context effects are compatible with a monograph-level preparation referent but do not prove it. High-frequency forms must receive reusable functions or classes, not narrow illnesses inferred from this example.

likely_failure: The manuscript may not encode recipients at all.
